meta.title: Word formation
meta.provenance: Built from the pantry seed (wordformation-v2.json) and the four Exam Traps batches (hotlist.js–hotlist4.js). Reviewed form by form in October 2026: two-step words given the word they are built FROM; real words that were listed as misspellings marked as confusables; the confide family rebuilt on confident; American spellings accepted for recognise. October 2026: 45 families added to fill the patterns Part 3 keeps testing (im-, -ship, -hood, -ise, -ness, -less, adverbs, person nouns), written for this app with examples on teenagers' interests; every sentence uses its exact word. October 2026: the full affix inventory of a B2–C1 coursebook appendix, 102 forms added so every group has at least three examples (re-, mis-, de-, inter-, out-, un- and -ate for verbs; non-, co-, ex-, -dom, -age, -al for nouns; non-, over-/under-, -ish, -ary/-ory for adjectives; -ward(s), -wise for adverbs), with a meaning for every group.

rules.title: Drop the e
rules.text: A silent e disappears before an ending that starts with a vowel: create + ive = creative.

rules.title: Keep the e
rules.text: Keep the e after c or g so the sound stays soft: courage + ous = courageous.

rules.title: y becomes i
rules.text: After a consonant, y changes to i before most endings: happy + ness = happiness, rely + able = reliable.

rules.title: Double the letter
rules.text: Some words double the last letter before an ending: sun + y = sunny. After a prefix, both letters stay: mis + spell = misspell.

rules.title: The stem changes
rules.text: Some words change inside before the ending. Learn the pair, not the rule: decide, decision. strong, strength.

rules.title: in- changes shape
rules.text: in- becomes im- before p or m, il- before l and ir- before r.

rules.title: Keep every letter
rules.text: A prefix or ending never removes a letter from the base: dis + satisfied, embarrass + ment.

un-.tip: The most common negative prefix. Use it with many adjectives and with verbs that reverse an action.

in-.tip: Often used with Latin-style words: inaccurate, incomplete. Changes to im-, il-, ir-.

im-.tip: in- before p or m: impatient, immature.

dis-.tip: Used with verbs and nouns: disagree, dishonest, disconnect.

mis-.tip: Something done in the wrong way: misunderstand, mislead.

re-.tip: Do something a second time: rebuild, rewrite.

over-.tip: overestimate, overreact. The opposite is under-.

-ion.tip: Makes nouns from verbs. The stem often changes: decide, decision.

-ation.tip: Makes nouns from verbs ending in -ate, -ise, or -ify: organise, organisation.

-ition.tip: Makes nouns from verbs like compete: competition.

-ive.tip: Makes adjectives from verbs: attractive, creative.

-ful.tip: Only one l. Careful, useful, successful.

-able.tip: More common than -ible. Use it with whole base words: enjoyable, reliable.

-ible.tip: Sounds the same as -able. Only the spelling tells you: accessible, visible.

-eous.tip: Keeps the e after g to keep the soft sound: courageous, outrageous.

-ious.tip: Often after the letters c, t or x: cautious, suspicious.

-ment.tip: Makes nouns from verbs. Keep the base letters: improvement, embarrassment.

-ness.tip: Makes nouns from adjectives: happiness, kindness.

-ity.tip: Makes nouns from adjectives: popularity, creativity.

-ance.meaning: the state of, the act of
-ance.tip: Sounds the same as -ence, so learn each noun: importance, appearance.

-ence.meaning: the state of, the act of

-ant.meaning: a person or thing that, having the quality of

-al.tip: Makes adjectives from nouns: environmental, national.

-ical.tip: Sometimes has a different meaning from -ic: economic and economical.

-ly.tip: Makes adverbs. Watch the spelling: happily, truly, gently.

-ise.tip: real, realise. British -ise or American -ize: Cambridge accepts both.

-en.tip: Makes verbs from adjectives: widen, strengthen.

-th.tip: Makes nouns, with a vowel change: long, length. deep, depth.

-ist.meaning: a person who does or studies

-ing.meaning: causing a feeling, or happening now
-ing.tip: Makes adjectives from verbs: confusing, embarrassing. Compare -ed: embarrassed means how you feel.

-ice.tip: choose becomes choice. Learn the pair, not a rule.

-ure.tip: please, pleasure. proceed, procedure (only one e after the c).

-ry.tip: Keep the whole base: rival, rivalry.

-etic.tip: energy becomes energetic. The y changes shape.

-ular.tip: spectacle becomes spectacular. Only one l.

-f.tip: prove becomes proof. Learn the pair, not a rule.

-ian.tip: guard, guardian: a person who protects.

de-.tip: deforestation has a prefix and a suffix: de + forest + ation.

-ship.tip: friend, friendship. member, membership. leader, leadership.

-hood.tip: child, childhood. neighbour, neighbourhood. Always two o's.

-ism.tip: critic, criticism. Keep the c of the base.

-istic.tip: real, realistic. The adverb adds -ally: realistically.

-itive.tip: sense, sensitive: easily upset. Not the same as sensible.

-ific.tip: science, scientific. The stem changes: scienc- becomes scient-.

-ledge.tip: know, knowledge. Learn the whole word: k-n-o-w-l-e-d-g-e.

-t.tip: high, height. Keep the e: h-e-i-g-h-t.

forms.gloss: a choice you make after thinking

forms.gloss: able to decide quickly and clearly
forms.teen: The captain made a decisive move in the last minute.

avoid.why: Wrong. decide loses -de and gains -s: de-cis-ion.
Wrong. decide loses -de and gains -s: de-cis-ive.

forms.gloss: the act of making something new

forms.teen: Her latest creation is a game about robots.
My friend is really creative and designs her own clothes.

forms.gloss: the ability to think of new ideas
forms.teen: Making videos gives me a way to show my creativity.

avoid.why: Wrong. Drop the e of create, then add -ive.
Wrong. Drop the e of create, then add -ion.

forms.gloss: something that makes people want to visit
forms.ex: The castle is a major tourist attraction.
forms.teen: The water park was the main attraction of the trip.

forms.gloss: pleasant to look at or interesting

avoid.why: Wrong. This verb takes -ive, not -ful.
Spelling. Keep both t: attract + ion.

forms.gloss: being unable to stop doing or using something
forms.ex: He is fighting an addiction to gambling.

forms.teen: Short videos are very addictive.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep both d: addict + ion.
Spelling. Keep both d: addict + ive.

forms.gloss: having a strong effect on people

forms.ex: The brand paid an influencer to advertise it.
forms.teen: My cousin wants to become an influencer.

avoid.why: Wrong. The c changes to t: influence, influential.
Wrong. A person who influences is an influencer.

forms.teen: The popularity of the game has exploded.
The new school rule is very unpopular.

avoid.why: Wrong. popular takes un-.
Wrong. The noun ending is -ity.

forms.gloss: harmful substances in air, water or soil
forms.ex: Air pollution is a serious problem.
forms.teen: Our class is studying plastic pollution in the sea.

forms.teen: Factories must reduce each pollutant they release.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep both l: pollute + ion.
Spelling. Keep both l: pollute + ant.

forms.gloss: able to continue without harming the environment

forms.gloss: the ability to continue for a long time without harm
forms.ex: The firm is proud of its sustainability record.
forms.teen: Sustainability is a hot topic at school.

avoid.why: Wrong. This one is -able.
Spelling. -able becomes -abil- before -ity.

forms.teen: Skating on the wet pavement is dangerous.

forms.ex: They would never endanger a child.
forms.teen: Hunting can endanger rare animals.

avoid.why: Wrong. Danger takes -ous.
Spelling. The ending is -ous, not -us.

forms.teen: It was courageous of her to speak up in class.

forms.gloss: give someone confidence to do something
forms.ex: Good teachers encourage shy pupils to speak up.
forms.teen: My coach tries to encourage everyone on the team.

altwhy.dis-: discourage is the opposite of encourage.

forms.gloss: make someone less willing to do something
forms.ex: High prices discourage people from buying.
forms.teen: Do not let one bad mark discourage you.

altwhy.en-: encourage is the opposite: to give confidence.

avoid.why: Wrong. Keep the e, so the g stays soft: courageous.
Wrong. The verb is encourage, with en-.

forms.teen: Be careful with my headphones.
A careless tackle gave away a penalty.
Read the question carefully before you answer.

avoid.why: Spelling. -ful has one l, even when you add -ly: careful + ly = carefully.
Spelling. -less has two s: care + less.

forms.teen: My phone is old and not very reliable.

forms.ex: Our reliance on oil is a problem.
forms.teen: Their reliance on social media worries teachers.

avoid.why: Wrong. y becomes i before -able.
Wrong. This noun ends in -ance.

forms.teen: The school trip was really enjoyable.
He plays guitar for pure enjoyment.

avoid.why: Wrong. y after a vowel stays y: enjoy + able.
Wrong. y after a vowel stays y: enjoy + ment.

forms.teen: Younger kids are dependent on their parents.

altwhy.-ant: -ant makes the noun (a dependant) in British English.

forms.ex: Dependence on foreign oil is risky.
forms.teen: Heavy dependence on screens affects sleep.
I want to be more independent this year.
Getting a bus pass gave me more independence.

avoid.why: Not for the adjective. In British English -ant is the noun (a dependant).
Wrong. The noun is -ence.

forms.teen: Drama club really built my confidence.

forms.gloss: in a way that shows you believe in yourself
forms.teen: He walked confidently onto the stage for his first solo.

forms.ex: He was overconfident and lost the match.
forms.teen: Don't be overconfident just because you won the first round.

avoid.why: Wrong. The noun ends -ence.
Wrong. confident + -ly: just add -ly. There is no -al- in it.

nodes.note: confident is the word to build from: -ent becomes -ence for the noun, and -ly makes the adverb.

forms.teen: We debated the economic effects of tourism.

altwhy.-ical: economical means cheap to run, not 'to do with the economy'.

forms.teen: A bus pass is more economical than paying each day.

altwhy.-ic: economic means to do with the economy.

avoid.why: Different word. economical means cheap to run; economic means to do with the economy.
Different word. economic is about the economy; economical means cheap to run.

nodes.note: Two adjectives, two meanings. economic = to do with the economy; economical = cheap to run.

forms.teen: The team won a historic title.

altwhy.-ical: historical means to do with the past; historic means important in history.

forms.teen: We watched a historical film about Rome.

altwhy.-ic: historic means important in history, not just 'about the past'.

avoid.why: Different word. historical means to do with the past; historic means important in history.
Different word. historic means important; historical means to do with the past.

nodes.note: historic = important in history; historical = to do with the past.

forms.gloss: a disagreement, or a set of reasons
forms.teen: Your argument needs more evidence.

avoid.why: Spelling. argue drops its e before -ment, an exception to the usual rule.
Spelling. The ending is -ment.

forms.teen: Her happiness was clear when she got the part.
The kids played happily all afternoon.
He was unhappy with his results.

forms.gloss: the state of not being happy
forms.teen: Her unhappiness at the new school was easy to see.

avoid.why: Wrong. y becomes i: happiness.
Wrong. y becomes i: happily.

forms.teen: Her biggest strength is staying calm.

Wrong. strong becomes strength- before -en.

forms.ex: Check the depth of the lake.
forms.teen: Divers explored the depth of the cave.

avoid.why: Wrong. deep becomes depth, with one e.
Spelling. Keep both e: deep + en.

forms.ex: We need to simplify the form.
forms.teen: Can you simplify the instructions?

forms.teen: She simply forgot her homework.

forms.ex: I like the simplicity of the design.
forms.teen: The simplicity of the game makes it fun.

Spelling. The noun ending is -ity: simplic + ity.

forms.ex: Can you clarify what you mean?
forms.teen: Could you clarify the task for us?

avoid.why: Wrong. clear to clarify is an irregular change.
Wrong. clear to clarity is an irregular change.

forms.teen: That was a truly amazing concert.
I told my mum the truth about the broken window.

avoid.why: Spelling. true drops its e: truly, an exception.
Spelling. true drops its e: truth.

forms.teen: Fortunately, I remembered my charger.
It was an unfortunate time to lose my phone.
Unfortunately, the match was cancelled.

avoid.why: Wrong. fortunate takes un-.
Wrong. fortunate takes un-.

forms.ex: She has been unemployed for a year.
forms.teen: My uncle was unemployed for a few months.
Many students look for part-time employment.

forms.gloss: a person or company that gives jobs
forms.teen: My employer lets me swap shifts.

forms.gloss: the state of not having a job
forms.teen: Youth unemployment is a big problem in many countries.

avoid.why: Wrong. Keep the base as it is: employ + ment.
Wrong. employ + er, with one e.
Wrong. employed takes un-.

forms.teen: I disagree with the teacher's choice.

forms.ex: The two sides reached an agreement.
forms.teen: We made an agreement to share the console.
She is an agreeable person to work with.

forms.gloss: a situation where people do not agree
forms.ex: There was a disagreement about the plan.
forms.teen: We had a disagreement about which film to watch.

avoid.why: Wrong. The opposite of agree is disagree.
Spelling. Keep both e: agree + able.
Spelling. The ending is -ment.

forms.ex: The tracks disappear in the snow.
forms.teen: My charger seems to disappear every week.
Do not judge a person by appearance.

avoid.why: Wrong. appear takes dis-.
Wrong. This noun ends -ance.
Spelling. dis + appear has one s then two p: disappear.

forms.ex: Do not overestimate your chances; the other team is stronger.
forms.teen: Do not overestimate how much you can learn the night before.

altwhy.under-: underestimate means to guess too low. This sentence warns against guessing too high.

forms.ex: Never underestimate her; she is smarter than she looks.
forms.teen: Never underestimate a small team.

altwhy.over-: overestimate means to guess too high. This sentence is about guessing too low.

avoid.why: Not natural. Use over- (too high) or under- (too low).
Not natural. Use over- (too high) or under- (too low).

forms.teen: Do not overreact to one bad comment online.

altwhy.under-: underreact is rare. The sentence warns against reacting too strongly.

forms.gloss: what you do or feel in response
forms.teen: His reaction to the news made everyone laugh.

avoid.why: Spelling. react + ion keeps the t: reaction.
Wrong. The noun is react + ion, nothing more.
Spelling. over + react keeps both r.

forms.teen: Downloading films without paying is illegal.

forms.gloss: in a way that is against the law
forms.teen: He was fined for riding illegally on the pavement.

avoid.why: Wrong. in- becomes il- before l.
Wrong. legal takes il-.
Spelling. Keep both l: il + legal.

forms.gloss: not careful about the results of your actions
forms.teen: Leaving the oven on was irresponsible.

forms.gloss: a duty to take care of something
forms.ex: She has a sense of responsibility.
forms.teen: Looking after the dog is my responsibility.

avoid.why: Wrong. responsible takes ir-.
Spelling. This one ends in -ible.
Spelling. Keep both r: ir + responsible.

forms.ex: The wire is invisible to the naked eye.
forms.teen: The ink is invisible until you use the light.

forms.ex: Visibility was poor in the fog.
forms.teen: Visibility was poor during the hike.

avoid.why: Wrong. visible takes in-.
Spelling. The ending is -ible.

forms.gloss: the right to keep things to yourself
forms.ex: Everyone has a right to privacy.
forms.teen: Check your privacy settings on every app.

forms.gloss: in a way others cannot see
forms.teen: She asked the teacher privately about her grade.

Spelling. Keep the e of private: private + ly.

forms.teen: Use a strong password for better security.

forms.ex: He felt insecure about his job.
forms.teen: Many teens feel insecure about their looks.

avoid.why: Possible in computing, but insecure is the standard word for feelings.
Spelling. The noun ending is -ity.

forms.ex: Always disconnect the power cable before cleaning the printer.
forms.teen: Disconnect from your phone for an hour before bed.
The Wi-Fi connection keeps dropping.

forms.ex: The towns interconnect by bus and rail.
forms.teen: All the levels interconnect, so you can go back at any time.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep both n: connect + ion.
Spelling. Keep both n: dis + connect.
Wrong. The opposite of connect is disconnect.

forms.teen: Our school is proud to be tolerant.

forms.ex: The school has zero tolerance for bullying.
forms.teen: Tolerance starts with listening.

avoid.why: Wrong. This adjective ends in -ant.
Wrong. This noun ends in -ance.

forms.teen: Talking to someone can reduce anxiety before a test.

avoid.why: Wrong. The noun is anxiety: anxi- + -ety.
Wrong. The noun is anxiety: anxi- + -ety.

forms.ex: His face turned red with embarrassment.
forms.teen: I felt real embarrassment when my phone rang in class.
That photo of me is so embarrassing.

avoid.why: Spelling. embarrass has two r and two s.
Spelling. embarrass has two r and two s.

forms.gloss: an unhappy feeling about what others have

avoid.why: Spelling. jealous keeps the -ou-: jealousy.
Not natural. The noun is jealousy.

forms.teen: Our school entered the robotics competition.

Wrong. compete becomes competit- before -ive.

forms.gloss: to do with nature and the planet
forms.teen: I joined the environmental club at school.

forms.ex: The environmentalist spoke at the protest.
forms.teen: She wants to become an environmentalist.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep the n before the m: environ + ment + al.
Spelling. Keep the n before the m: environ + ment + alist.

forms.teen: Online, stay respectful even when you disagree.

avoid.why: Spelling. -ful has one l.
Wrong. respectful takes dis-.

Wrong. The noun is choice.

forms.teen: I noticed a lot of growth in my little brother this year.

forms.gloss: to grow too big or old for something

Wrong. The noun is growth.

forms.gloss: the time of life when you are young

forms.teen: Youth clubs give teenagers somewhere to meet.

avoid.why: Wrong. young becomes youth.
Spelling. Keep the o: youth.

forms.ex: Measure the length of the table.
forms.teen: The length of the film made me fall asleep.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep the g: length.
Wrong. long becomes length.

forms.gloss: a set way of doing something
forms.ex: Follow the correct procedure in an emergency.
forms.teen: The school has a procedure for reporting problems.

avoid.why: Spelling. proceed becomes procedure, with only one e after the c.
Spelling. The noun ends in -ure.

forms.ex: There was a significant rise in prices.
forms.teen: A significant number of students walk to school.

forms.gloss: the importance or meaning of something

forms.ex: It was a pleasure to meet you.
forms.teen: Playing football is a real pleasure after a long week.

forms.ex: We spent a pleasant afternoon in the park.
forms.teen: The new teacher is really pleasant.

Wrong. successful takes un-.

forms.teen: The instructions were completely incomprehensible.

Spelling. This one ends in -ible.

forms.teen: Her generosity helped the whole team.

forms.ex: The company is in financial trouble.

Wrong. This noun ends in -or.

forms.teen: My teacher wrote me a reference for my part-time job.

avoid.why: Wrong. This noun ends in -ence.
Spelling. One r in the middle: reference.

forms.gloss: a wrong idea that many people believe
forms.ex: It is a misconception that bats are blind.
forms.teen: There is a misconception that gamers never go outside.

avoid.why: Wrong. The prefix is mis-.
Spelling. One s after mi: mis + conception.

forms.gloss: sending a signal or message, or passing on a disease
forms.ex: The transmission of the signal was delayed.
forms.teen: The transmission of the match was cut off.

avoid.why: Spelling. transmit becomes transmission, with -ssion.
Spelling. Keep both s: transmission.

forms.ex: A wealthy family owned the castle.
forms.teen: He became wealthy by selling apps.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep the ea of wealth: wealthy.
Wrong. wealth takes -y.

forms.ex: Measure the width of the door.
forms.teen: The width of the road makes it safe for bikes.

forms.ex: They plan to widen the road.
forms.teen: Reading will widen your vocabulary.

avoid.why: Spelling. The order is d, t, h: width.
Wrong. wide becomes width.
Spelling. One d: widen.

forms.ex: This film is suitable for children.
forms.teen: Flip-flops are not suitable for a long hike.

forms.ex: Those shoes are unsuitable for hiking.
forms.teen: The film was unsuitable for young children.

avoid.why: Spelling. This one ends in -able.
Wrong. suitable takes un-.

forms.ex: The death of the king shocked the country.
forms.teen: Nobody was ready for the death of the old school oak tree.

avoid.why: Wrong. die becomes death.
Spelling. Keep the a: death.

forms.gloss: facts that show something is true
forms.ex: Do you have any proof of your claim?
forms.teen: I need proof that you finished your homework.

forms.ex: Scientists tried to disprove the theory.
forms.teen: Nobody could disprove her argument.

avoid.why: Wrong. The noun is proof.
Spelling. disprove has one o after the r.
Wrong. The opposite of prove is disprove.

forms.gloss: a person who looks after someone or protects something
forms.ex: The court named her aunt as guardian.
forms.teen: My guardian picks me up after school.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep the u: guardian.
Wrong. This noun ends in -ian.

forms.ex: Deforestation destroys the homes of many animals.
forms.teen: Our geography project is about deforestation in the Amazon.

avoid.why: Spelling. Only one r: forest.
Wrong. The prefix is de-.

forms.teen: My phone battery lasts extraordinarily long.

avoid.why: Wrong. y becomes i: extraordinarily.
Spelling. extra + ordinary: extraordinarily.

forms.teen: Homework is manageable if you plan ahead.

forms.gloss: the people or skill of running something
forms.teen: Time management helps me before exams.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep the e after g: manageable.
Spelling. Keep the e of manage: management.

forms.gloss: the time after you stop working
forms.ex: He is looking forward to retirement.
forms.teen: My grandad's retirement party was huge.

avoid.why: Spelling. Keep the e of retire: retirement.
Wrong. The noun is retirement.

forms.ex: It is impossible to finish this in an hour.
forms.teen: That level is impossible without the double jump.

forms.ex: There is a possibility of rain later.
forms.teen: There's a real possibility the match will be cancelled.

forms.ex: It will possibly be ready tomorrow.
forms.teen: This could possibly be the best song of the year.

avoid.why: Wrong. Before p, the negative prefix is im-: impossible.
Wrong. possible becomes possibil- + -ity: possibility.

forms.ex: Don't be so impatient; the bus will come.
forms.teen: I get impatient when a video won't load.
Building the whole Lego city took a lot of patience.

forms.ex: She waited patiently for her turn.
forms.teen: He waited patiently in the queue for the new trainers.

forms.ex: She could not hide her impatience.
forms.teen: My impatience gets worse when the Wi-Fi is slow.

avoid.why: Wrong. Before p, use im-: impatient.
Wrong. patient ends in -ent, so the noun ends in -ence.

forms.ex: It is impolite to interrupt people.
forms.teen: Leaving the group chat without a word felt impolite.
Her politeness made a great first impression at the interview.
She politely asked them to turn the music down.

avoid.why: Wrong. Before p, use im-: impolite.
Wrong. Keep the e: polite + -ness.

forms.ex: The plan is imperfect but it will work.
forms.teen: My drawing is imperfect, but I like it.

forms.ex: She cooks every dish to perfection.
forms.teen: He practised the trick until he reached perfection.
The goalkeeper timed his jump perfectly.

avoid.why: Wrong. Before p, use im-: imperfect.
Wrong. perfect keeps its t: perfec-t-ion.

forms.teen: Posting that joke was really immature.

forms.ex: She showed great maturity for her age.
forms.teen: He handled losing the final with real maturity.

avoid.why: Wrong. Before m, use im-: immature.
Wrong. The ending is -ity: maturity.

forms.teen: Our friendship started in a gaming chat.
The new player was friendly to everyone on the team.
The comments under her video were really unfriendly.

avoid.why: Wrong. i before e here: fr-i-e-nd.
Wrong. friend keeps its i: friend-ly.

forms.gloss: the time when you are a child
forms.teen: I spent my childhood playing football in the street.

forms.gloss: behaving like a child, in a bad way
forms.teen: Arguing about the last slice of pizza was childish.

forms.ex: They were childless for many years.
forms.teen: The old couple next door are childless but love our dog.

avoid.why: Wrong. The suffix is -hood, with two o's.

forms.teen: There's a new skate park in my neighbourhood.

forms.ex: They moved to a neighbouring town.
forms.teen: We played against a school from a neighbouring village.

avoid.why: Wrong. The area is a neighbourhood: -hood, not -ship.

forms.gloss: being a member of a group
forms.ex: Membership of the club costs £20 a year.
forms.teen: My gym membership runs out next month.

avoid.why: Wrong. Belonging to a club is membership: -ship.

forms.teen: Our team leader planned every move.
Good leadership won us the tournament.
The headline was totally misleading.

forms.gloss: to make someone believe something false
forms.ex: The advert tried to mislead customers.
forms.teen: Edited photos can mislead your followers.

avoid.why: Wrong. Build it from leader: leader + -ship.
Wrong. One s: mis- + leading.

forms.ex: I didn't realise it was so late.
forms.teen: I didn't realise my mic was on the whole time.
Virtual reality headsets are getting cheaper.
The graphics in the new game are incredibly realistic.
Finishing the whole series in one night is unrealistic.

avoid.why: Wrong. real + -istic: realistic.
unreal is a real word, but it means strange, not impossible to achieve.

forms.gloss: to say what is wrong with something
forms.teen: Some fans criticise the ending of the series.
The new update received a lot of criticism.

forms.gloss: saying what is wrong; very important
forms.ex: She was critical of the plan.
forms.teen: The last minute of the match was critical.

avoid.why: Wrong. Keep the c of critic: criti-c-ise.
Wrong. The ending is -ism: criticism.

forms.ex: She wants to specialise in law.
forms.teen: He wants to specialise in goalkeeping.

forms.ex: See a specialist about your knee.
forms.teen: A games specialist reviewed the new console.

avoid.why: Wrong. The person suffix is -ist: specialist.

forms.gloss: to learn something so you remember it exactly
forms.teen: I can memorise a whole song in a day.
The final was the most memorable match of the season.

avoid.why: Wrong. memory loses its y: memor- + -able.

forms.gloss: feeling that something good will happen
forms.ex: We are hopeful about the result.
forms.teen: The coach is hopeful about Saturday's game.

forms.gloss: with no chance of success; very bad at something
forms.teen: I'm hopeless at drawing.

forms.gloss: used to say what you hope will happen
forms.teen: Hopefully the update comes out this week.

avoid.why: Wrong. The suffix -ful has only one l.
Wrong. hopeful + -ly gives two l's: hopefully.

forms.teen: These shortcuts are useful for gaming.
My phone is useless without Wi-Fi.
Every user gets a free skin.
You can reuse the same password reset link only once.

forms.gloss: to use in a wrong or harmful way
forms.teen: Don't misuse the chat to insult other players.

avoid.why: Wrong. The suffix -ful has only one l.
Wrong. The suffix is -less, with two s's.

forms.teen: The tutorial was really helpful.

forms.gloss: not useful or willing to help
forms.teen: The comments on my post were unhelpful.
I felt helpless watching my team lose.

avoid.why: Wrong. The suffix -ful has only one l.

forms.ex: We need more awareness of the problem.
forms.teen: The campaign raised awareness of online safety.

forms.ex: He was unaware of the danger.
forms.teen: I was unaware the stream had started.

avoid.why: Wrong. The noun is aware + -ness.

forms.teen: A small act of kindness can change someone's day.

forms.ex: That was an unkind thing to say.
forms.teen: Unkind comments online can really hurt.

avoid.why: Wrong. No extra e: kind + -ness.

forms.gloss: a lack of strength; a fault
forms.ex: His only weakness is his temper.
forms.teen: Defending is my biggest weakness.

forms.ex: Too much sugar can weaken your teeth.
forms.teen: Losing our captain will weaken the team.

avoid.why: Wrong. No extra e: weak + -ness.

forms.gloss: being sad because you are alone
forms.ex: Loneliness is a problem for many old people.
forms.teen: Moving to a new school can bring loneliness at first.

avoid.why: Wrong. The y becomes i before -ness: loneliness.

forms.gloss: a belief about what will happen
forms.ex: There is an expectation that students do their homework.
forms.teen: The new album lived up to every expectation.
The plot twist was completely unexpected.
Our team unexpectedly won the cup.

avoid.why: Wrong. Build it from unexpected: unexpected + -ly.

forms.teen: It's surprising how fast she learned the guitar.

forms.gloss: in a way that is surprising
forms.teen: The cheap headphones sound surprisingly good.

avoid.why: Wrong. Don't forget the first r: sur-prise.

forms.ex: There is increasing interest in the subject.
forms.teen: An increasing number of teenagers play chess online.
Esports are increasingly popular.

avoid.why: Wrong. Keep the g: increasing + -ly.

forms.ex: You were lucky to find a seat.
forms.teen: I was lucky to get tickets for the concert.
Luckily, I'd saved the game before it crashed.
Unluckily, the ball hit the post.

avoid.why: Wrong. lucky + -ly: the y becomes i, so luckily.

forms.gloss: a person who works in science
forms.ex: A scientist is studying the virus.
forms.teen: She wants to be a scientist who studies space.
The video explains the scientific reason why ice floats.

avoid.why: Wrong. science becomes scient- + -ist: scientist.

forms.teen: My cousin is a musician in a rock band.

forms.gloss: connected with music; good at music
forms.ex: She comes from a musical family.
forms.teen: He's very musical and plays three instruments.

avoid.why: Wrong. music + -ian: musician, with an i before the a.

forms.gloss: a person whose job is in politics
forms.teen: A local politician visited our school.
We discussed a political issue in class.

avoid.why: Wrong. politic- + -ian: politician.

forms.gloss: a person who acts in films or plays
forms.teen: The actor posted a video from the film set.
Staying active helps you sleep better.

forms.gloss: something you do for fun or work
forms.teen: Climbing is my favourite weekend activity.
My account was inactive for months.

forms.ex: The app lets students interact with their teacher.
forms.teen: In this game you can interact with players all over the world.

forms.ex: You need a code to activate the card.
forms.teen: Tap twice to activate your shield.
I had to deactivate my account for a week.

avoid.why: Wrong. A person who acts is an actor: -or.
Wrong. active takes in-: inactive.

forms.ex: She has the ability to learn fast.
forms.teen: He has an amazing ability to read the game.
I was unable to log in all morning.

forms.gloss: a condition that limits what someone can do
forms.ex: The building is accessible for people with a disability.
forms.teen: The Paralympics celebrate athletes with a disability.

forms.ex: The scholarship will enable her to study abroad.
forms.teen: This setting will enable you to play offline.

forms.gloss: not being able to do something
forms.ex: His inability to swim worried his parents.
forms.teen: My inability to wake up early is a family joke.

avoid.why: Wrong. able becomes abil- + -ity: ability.
Wrong. able takes un-: unable.

forms.teen: Saving some pocket money is sensible.

forms.ex: She is sensitive about her height.
forms.teen: My teeth are sensitive to cold drinks.
Fighting over a game is senseless.

forms.gloss: something that has no meaning or is not true
forms.teen: The rumour about our teacher was total nonsense.

avoid.why: sensitive is a real word, but it means easily upset; sensible means showing good judgement.
Wrong. The ending is -ible: sensible.

forms.ex: She has a good knowledge of history.
forms.teen: His knowledge of football history is amazing.

forms.ex: He is very knowledgeable about cars.
forms.teen: The shop assistant was really knowledgeable about phones.
An unknown player scored the winning goal.

avoid.why: Wrong. Don't forget the d: know-l-e-d-g-e.
Wrong. Keep the e: knowledge + -able.

forms.gloss: an opinion about what someone should do
forms.ex: Can you give me some advice?
forms.teen: My older brother gave me advice about exams.

forms.ex: It is advisable to book early.
forms.teen: It's advisable to back up your files.

avoid.why: advise is the verb; the noun is advice, with a c.
Wrong. Drop the e: advis- + -able.

forms.ex: The two cities are very different.
forms.teen: My sister and I have very different taste in music.

forms.gloss: the way two things are not the same
forms.teen: Practice makes a big difference to your score.

avoid.why: Wrong. differ has two f's: difference.
Wrong. different ends in -ent, so the noun ends in -ence.

forms.ex: Do you have a preference for tea or coffee?
forms.teen: My preference is for games with a good story.
Studying in the morning is preferable for me.

avoid.why: Wrong. The noun ends in -ence: preference.
Wrong. Only one f, and only one r before -able: preferable.

forms.gloss: looking at how things are alike or different
forms.ex: There is no comparison between them.
forms.teen: In comparison with last year, the tickets are cheap.

forms.ex: The new phone is a comparative bargain.
forms.teen: We studied comparative adjectives in English.

forms.gloss: fairly, when compared with something else
forms.teen: The game is comparatively cheap for what you get.

avoid.why: Wrong. compare becomes compar- + -ison: comparison.

forms.gloss: what you say to make something clear
forms.ex: There is no explanation for it.
forms.teen: The video gives a clear explanation of the rules.

avoid.why: Wrong. explain loses its i: expla-n-ation.

forms.gloss: words that say what something is like
forms.teen: The description of the hotel was better than the real thing.

forms.ex: Use descriptive language in your story.
forms.teen: Her descriptive writing won the school prize.

avoid.why: Wrong. It starts with de-: description.
Wrong. The b becomes p: descri-p-tion.

forms.gloss: how tall or high something is
forms.ex: What is the height of the wall?
forms.teen: Basketball players are usually above average height.

forms.ex: The music helps to heighten the tension.
forms.teen: The final scene will heighten the suspense.

avoid.why: Wrong. Keep the e: h-e-i-g-h-t.
Wrong for size: how tall something is, is its height.

forms.teen: The remix is good, but the original song is better.
The game was originally made for one player.

avoid.why: Wrong. No extra i or o: orig-in-al.
Wrong. original + -ly gives two l's: originally.

forms.ex: It is natural to feel nervous.
forms.teen: It's natural to be nervous before a match.
The character's movements look unnatural in the trailer.

forms.gloss: as you would expect; not in an artificial way
forms.teen: Some people are naturally good at languages.

avoid.why: Wrong. natural + -ly gives two l's: naturally.
Wrong. natural takes un-: unnatural.

forms.gloss: pleasant to wear or sit on; relaxed
forms.teen: This gaming chair is really comfortable.
I felt uncomfortable speaking in front of the class.

avoid.why: Wrong. comfort starts with com-: comfortable.
Wrong. The ending is -able: comfortable.

forms.ex: Honesty is important in a friendship.
forms.teen: I appreciate your honesty about my song.

forms.ex: It was dishonest to copy his homework.
forms.teen: Cheating in an online game is dishonest.

avoid.why: Wrong. honest takes dis-: dishonest.
Wrong. honest + -y: honesty.

forms.teen: My sleep has been irregular since the holidays.
I check my messages regularly.

avoid.why: Wrong. Before r, the negative is ir-: irregular.
Wrong. ir- + regular gives two r's: irregular.

forms.ex: She has a good understanding of maths.
forms.teen: Thanks for your understanding when I was late.
A misunderstanding in the group chat started the argument.

forms.ex: Don't misunderstand me — I like the idea.
forms.teen: People often misunderstand jokes in a text message.

avoid.why: Wrong. One s: mis- + understanding.

forms.gloss: to write again, usually to improve
forms.teen: I had to rewrite my essay after the teacher's comments.

avoid.why: No hyphen: re- joins the verb as one word.

forms.ex: They will replay the match next week.
forms.teen: Let me replay that goal in slow motion.

forms.ex: They plan to rebuild the bridge.
forms.teen: It took weeks to rebuild my Minecraft castle.

forms.gloss: a structure with walls and a roof
forms.ex: The new building has twenty floors.
forms.teen: Our school building is over a hundred years old.

forms.gloss: to treat waste so it can be used again
forms.teen: Our school wants to recycle all its plastic bottles.

avoid.why: Keep the y of cycle: re-cycle.

forms.gloss: to remove the ice from something frozen
forms.ex: Defrost the chicken before you cook it.
forms.teen: I forgot to defrost the pizza, so we ordered one.

forms.gloss: to find the meaning of something written in code
forms.teen: It took us an hour to decode the clue in the escape room.

forms.gloss: to be more in number than
forms.ex: Girls outnumber boys in the drama club.
forms.teen: In the final, the home fans outnumber the visitors.
Tortoises can outlive their owners.

forms.gloss: to reverse what has been done
forms.ex: Press Ctrl+Z to undo the last change.
forms.teen: You can't undo a message once everyone has read it.

forms.gloss: to open with a key or code
forms.ex: Use your fingerprint to unlock the phone.
forms.teen: Win three matches to unlock a new character.

forms.gloss: to take things out of a bag or box
forms.ex: We were too tired to unpack.
forms.teen: I still haven't had time to unpack my suitcase.

forms.gloss: a parcel; a set of things sold together
forms.teen: The holiday package includes flights and a hotel.

forms.gloss: to improve the quality of something
forms.teen: Travelling will enrich your life more than any game.

forms.gloss: to give someone the confidence or right to do something
forms.ex: The project aims to empower young people.
forms.teen: Learning to code can empower you to build your own apps.

avoid.why: Before p, en- becomes em-: empower.

forms.gloss: to sleep longer than you intended
forms.ex: Don't oversleep on the day of the exam.
forms.teen: I always oversleep on Mondays.
If you overcook the eggs, they go rubbery.

forms.gloss: to cook for too short a time
forms.ex: It is dangerous to undercook chicken.
forms.teen: Try not to undercook the burgers at the barbecue.

forms.gloss: to ask for too much money
forms.ex: The taxi driver tried to overcharge us.
forms.teen: Some sites overcharge for concert tickets.

forms.gloss: to ask for too little money
forms.teen: Check the bill: cafés sometimes undercharge you by accident.

forms.gloss: to exchange or put each in the place of the other
forms.ex: You can interchange the two parts.
forms.teen: In this game you can interchange weapons with your teammates.

forms.gloss: to officially check or prove that something is correct
forms.ex: You must validate your ticket before boarding.
forms.teen: Tap here to validate your email address.

forms.gloss: to make someone want to do something
forms.teen: Music helps me motivate myself to study.

avoid.why: The verb ending is -ate: motivate.

forms.teen: The pressure will intensify as the final gets closer.

avoid.why: Drop the e and add -ify: intensify.

forms.ex: Volunteers helped to beautify the park.
forms.teen: We used plants to beautify our classroom.

avoid.why: The y of beauty becomes i: beautify.

forms.ex: There is no certainty that it will work.
forms.teen: I can say with certainty that this is my favourite song.

forms.gloss: a state of not knowing what will happen
forms.ex: There is uncertainty about the future.
forms.teen: The uncertainty before the results is the worst part.
I'm uncertain about which subjects to choose next year.

avoid.why: certain + -ty: no extra i, uncertainty.

forms.ex: Sherlock Holmes is a fictional detective.
forms.teen: My favourite fictional character is from a manga.

forms.gloss: books about real facts and events
forms.teen: The library has a big non-fiction section about space.
My grandfather was a smoker for forty years.

forms.gloss: a person who does not smoke
forms.ex: As a non-smoker, she hates smoky rooms.
forms.teen: Every non-smoker in our family is glad the café is smoke-free.

forms.gloss: all the people living in a place
forms.ex: The population of the city is growing.
forms.teen: The population of my town doubles in the summer.

forms.gloss: too many people living in a place
forms.teen: Overpopulation is one of the topics in our geography project.

forms.gloss: extra time worked after the usual hours; extra time in a game
forms.teen: The match went into overtime.

forms.ex: We took the underground to the museum.
forms.teen: The underground in London is called the Tube.

forms.ex: Each worker at the factory has a badge.
forms.teen: Every worker at the shop wears a green T-shirt.

forms.ex: She went to lunch with a co-worker.
forms.teen: My mum's co-worker gave me a lift to school.

forms.gloss: a person who starts an organisation
forms.ex: The founder of the company is only thirty.
forms.teen: The founder of the app started it as a school project.

forms.gloss: one of the people who start an organisation together
forms.ex: He is a co-founder of the charity.
forms.teen: She is the co-founder of a popular gaming channel.

forms.gloss: the second pilot who helps fly a plane
forms.teen: In the game you can switch to the co-pilot seat.

forms.gloss: a person who was president before
forms.teen: An ex-president visited our city last month.

forms.gloss: a person who was champion before
forms.ex: The ex-champion lost in the first round.
forms.teen: The ex-champion now coaches young players.

forms.gloss: a man who used to be someone's boyfriend
forms.ex: She is still friends with her ex-boyfriend.
forms.teen: Her ex-boyfriend was in the same class.

forms.gloss: worth a lot of money; very useful
forms.teen: Your feedback is valuable to us.
The tutorials were invaluable when I learned to edit videos.

forms.gloss: a judgement of how much something is worth
forms.ex: The valuation of the house was high.
forms.teen: An expert gave a valuation of my grandad's old guitar.

forms.gloss: a fall in the value of something, especially money
forms.ex: The devaluation of the currency raised prices.
forms.teen: After the devaluation, holidays abroad became expensive.

avoid.why: There is no unvaluable: invaluable means extremely useful.

forms.teen: Good hydration helps you play better.

forms.gloss: a dangerous lack of water in the body
forms.ex: He was taken to hospital with dehydration.
forms.teen: Dehydration can make you feel dizzy in a long match.

forms.ex: His behaviour in class has improved.
forms.teen: Bad behaviour online can get your account banned.
Any misbehaviour on the school trip means no more trips.

avoid.why: Don't forget the i: behav-i-our.

forms.gloss: the right to act or speak as you want
forms.teen: Getting a phone gave me a lot more freedom.

forms.ex: He played games out of boredom.
forms.teen: Boredom is the worst part of a long car journey.

avoid.why: The suffix is -dom: boredom.

forms.gloss: good judgement that comes from experience
forms.ex: Grandparents have a lot of wisdom.
forms.teen: Her words of wisdom helped me before the exam.

avoid.why: The e disappears and the s stays: wisdom.

forms.gloss: the business of holidays and travel
forms.teen: Tourism brings thousands of visitors to the island every summer.

forms.ex: A tourist asked us for directions.
forms.teen: Every tourist wants a photo at the top of the hill.

forms.ex: The firefighter was praised for his heroism.
forms.teen: The film is about the heroism of ordinary people.

forms.gloss: the relationship between two people who are married
forms.teen: My grandparents' marriage started with a dance.

avoid.why: marry + -age: the y becomes i, so marriage.

forms.ex: My phone has no storage left.
forms.teen: I need more storage for all my photos.

forms.gloss: a lack of something that is needed
forms.ex: There is a shortage of water.
forms.teen: There's a shortage of tickets for the final.

forms.gloss: the act of coming to a place
forms.teen: The arrival of the new console made everyone excited.
His refusal to share the ball annoyed the team.

forms.ex: The animals' survival depends on the forest.
forms.teen: Survival games are really popular this year.
We played non-stop for three hours.

forms.ex: The film is too violent for children.
forms.teen: Some games are too violent for younger players.
The students organised a non-violent protest about climate change.

forms.ex: Alcoholic drinks are not sold to under-18s.
forms.teen: Alcoholic drinks are banned at the festival.

forms.ex: Would you like a non-alcoholic cocktail?
forms.teen: All the drinks at the school disco were non-alcoholic.

forms.gloss: how heavy someone or something is
forms.ex: What is the weight of the parcel?
forms.teen: Lifting weight at the gym is my brother's hobby.

forms.ex: The doctor said he was overweight.
forms.teen: Sitting all day can make people overweight.

forms.ex: The puppy was underweight when we found it.
forms.teen: Some models are dangerously underweight.

avoid.why: e before i here: w-e-i-g-h-t.

forms.teen: The bus is always crowded after school.
The concert was so overcrowded that we couldn't move.
The canteen is too noisy to talk.

avoid.why: Drop the e: nois- + -y, noisy.

forms.teen: On a sunny day the whole class wants to be outside.

avoid.why: Short vowel: double the n, sunny.

forms.ex: It was foolish to swim alone.
forms.teen: It was foolish to post my address online.

forms.ex: Don't be so selfish — share the sweets.
forms.teen: It's selfish to keep the ball to yourself all match.
Those trainers are really stylish.

forms.gloss: the ability to form pictures and ideas in your mind
forms.teen: You need a lot of imagination to write fantasy stories.

forms.gloss: not real, existing only in the mind
forms.teen: My little sister has an imaginary friend.

forms.gloss: full of new and original ideas
forms.ex: She is a very imaginative writer.
forms.teen: His imaginative drawings won the art prize.

avoid.why: imaginative is a real word, but it means full of ideas; imaginary means not real.

forms.gloss: the pleasant feeling when you get what you want
forms.teen: Finishing a hard level gives me real satisfaction.
My report said my progress was satisfactory.
The ending of the series was unsatisfactory for most fans.

avoid.why: The ending is -ory: satisfactory.

forms.teen: That guitarist is legendary among rock fans.
Can you say the alphabet backwards?
The balloon floated upwards into the sky.

forms.ex: We had dinner and went out afterwards.
